items.readable_text:
Content:
A reflection can be thought of as "mirroring" or "flipping" an object over a line of reflection.

Content:
When a point is reflected in the [MATH: x]-axis, the [MATH: x]-coordinate remains the same, but the [MATH: y]-coordinate is transformed into its opposite (i.e., its sign is changed). The following function can represent this transformation:

Content:
[MATH: (x,y) \mapsto (x,-y)]

Content:
For example, reflecting the point [MATH: P(3,2)] in the [MATH: x]-axis gives the point [MATH: Q(3,-2),] as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/8a63c15cc67067132f3d4701b913d162]

Content:
On the other hand, when a point is reflected in the [MATH: y]-axis, the [MATH: y]-coordinate remains the same, but the [MATH: x]-coordinate is transformed into its opposite (its sign is changed). The following function can represent this transformation:

Content:
[MATH: (x,y) \mapsto (-x,y)]

Content:
For example, reflecting the point [MATH: P(3,2)] in the [MATH: y]-axis gives the point [MATH: R(-3,2),] as shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/69815e3ca66e69298574bd4bd941ec1d]
